blocks.x: IoT, Twin & Robotics, tuned inside Agriculture & Food Systems: sector-specific design decisions, the delivery pattern with named owners, and outcomes gated on signed metrics.

In Agriculture & Food Systems, iot, digital twin & robotics bridges the physical and digital enterprise: industrial sensor network, digital twin platforms, computer vision and edge ai, predictive maintenance, robotics and autonomous systems integration, connected products, and smart infrastructure. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: industrial iot & sensor network, digital twin platform engineering, computer vision & edge ai — delivered on Dataq Twinverse and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Agronomic decisions run on tradition because soil, weather and crop telemetry are patchy; input spend is uniform where it should be variable.
Origin, organic and deforestation-free claims face EUDR-grade scrutiny; evidence is paper and trust.
Harvest forecasting is regional guesswork; quality attributes (protein, moisture, defects) are discovered at intake, not predicted.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

Delivery composes 7 services from the IoT, Digital Twin & Robotics tower — Industrial IoT & sensor network, Digital Twin Platform Engineering, Computer Vision & Edge AI, Predictive Maintenance & Asset Intelligence as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method, with EUDR obligations shaping the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Sense everything that matters: retrofit-friendly sensor network with governed telemetry.
Simulate before you cut steel: plant, fleet and product twins with governed physics and data.
Cameras into instruments: inspection, safety and counting at the edge, inside policy.
Fix it before it fails: RUL models wired into planning, spare parts and work orders.
Soil, weather and crop sensing with governance (variable-rate practice enabled)
Silo/supply-chain environment monitoring (quality preserved; losses down)

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: EUDR and EUDR. Deforestation-free due diligence with geolocation evidence for in-scope commodities. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Programs run on the fixed rhythm below, chosen so progress is legible from week one. Weeks 1–2 are measurement only: we lock the current metric with your team and both sides sign it before a line of build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a named control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 turn what worked into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, then report the measured delta against the baseline. A missed gate means a documented stop-or-redirect decision, not a quiet extension.
